results.prompt: Explain gradient checkpointing and what it trades away.
results.text:
Gradient checkpointing is a technique used in deep learning to reduce the memory usage of a model during training. It works by storing only the gradients of the model's parameters at certain points in time, rather than storing the entire model state. This is useful when training large models that don't fit in memory.
Gradient checkpointing trades away the ability to backpropagate gradients through time, which means that the gradients stored at each checkpoint are only valid for a short period of time.
